decision.reason: Robot 0 appears to support the outer rim; robot 1 supports the hand-side rim. Shift both robot-left about 7 cm to align the probable hem opening with the raised hand, then reassess cloth following and clearance. Hand entry is not yet established.

Cloth followed both grippers during the last shift. Robot 0 supports the outer rim; robot 1 guides the hand-side rim. Move both another short distance robot-left to reduce the visible hand–opening offset; entry remains unconfirmed.

Robot 0 retains outer support; robot 1 retains the hand-side rim. Two lateral corrections have not established entry. Hold both bases and reshape the probable hem opening by slightly raising robot 0’s edge and lowering robot 1’s edge toward the visible hand.

Robot 0 supports the higher outer rim; robot 1 supports the lowered hand-side rim. The same visible hand remains left and below the probable hem opening. Move both left and slightly down to reduce that gap, then inspect before attempting rim crossing.

Robot 0 maintains upper-rim support; robot 1 guides the near rim, with cloth still following both. Make a short leftward, slightly forward and downward hem-entry attempt toward the same visible hand. Recheck the hand against the rim; crossing is not yet established.

Robot 0 supports the outer rim; robot 1 holds the near rim. The hand is partly hidden by robot 1’s jaw without a visible rim crossing. Halt base advance and turn both wrists slightly to expose the hand–rim relationship while preserving support.

Robot 0 retains outer-rim support; robot 1 retains near-rim support. The wrist turn did not reveal a hand crossing the opening. Retract and raise both held edges a few centimeters to clear the hand and restore visibility before another entry attempt.

Robot 0 supports the higher rim; robot 1 controls the near rim. The target hand is visible again just left of that rim in robot 1’s head view. Make one short left/down entry motion, then check whether the hand lies between the opening’s rims.

Robot 0 supports the higher outer corner; robot 1 guides the near corner. The hand is adjacent to the yellow rim, but crossing remains unclear. Make one small leftward, forward and downward correction, then require visible rim-crossing evidence before further threading.

Both robots still support their respective rim sections, but two entry corrections have not shown a clear crossing. Pause forward and downward motion. Move robot 0 slightly outward and robot 1 left to gently widen the opening and expose the hand beside robot 1’s jaw.

Robot 0 and robot 1 retain opposite corners. Spreading narrowed the visible opening, and hand crossing remains unconfirmed. Ease the corners inward and pitch the held rim toward the mannequin, raising both lifts to limit downward movement while reshaping.
